title: Copilot draft PR publish guard in copilot-agent.yml: opened-with-changes vs empty-draft wait
answers: Copilot draft PR never gets marked ready for review
when does the copilot agent publish its draft pull request
Copilot opened a PR with changes but it stayed draft
Copilot agent empty draft waits for review request
body:
Symptom: A Copilot-authored PR that already contains file changes stays in draft, so reviewers never see it until someone manually clicks "Ready for review".
Root cause: .github/workflows/copilot-agent.yml:publish-draft only ran on pull_request_target `review_requested` events, so a PR opened with changes was never evaluated.
Fix pattern: Keep the trigger list `[opened, review_requested]` and gate the job's `if:` per action: `opened` publishes only when `github.event.pull_request.changed_files > 0`; `review_requested` publishes only when `github.event.sender.login == 'Copilot'`.
Constraints: Empty opened drafts must keep waiting for a Copilot-originated review_requested event, so do not drop the sender check or the changed_files check. Keep the identity guards (`pull_request.user.login == 'Copilot'` and `user.type == 'Bot'`) and the draft guard on every branch; the job must not publish human-authored drafts.
applies: Only the publish-draft job condition in .github/workflows/copilot-agent.yml; other jobs in that workflow are not covered by this note.
says: Copilot pull requests containing file changes stay stuck in draft instead of opening for review.
Automatically mark pull requests opened by the coding assistant as ready for review.
Draft pull requests created with changes never notify reviewers until manually published.
Empty draft pull requests from Copilot should not publish until review is explicitly requested.
Reviewers never see pull requests opened by Copilot because they stay in draft status.

The workflow triggers on [opened, review_requested], publishing an opened event only when github.event.pull_request.changed_files > 0, and publishing a review_requested event only when github.event.sender.login == 'Copilot'. Empty opened drafts must continue waiting for a Copilot-originated review request without removing sender or changed-file checks. Identity guards (pull_request.user.login == 'Copilot' and user.type == 'Bot') and draft guards must remain on all branches to avoid publishing human-authored drafts.
